holidays.name: International Polar Bear Day
holidays.description: A day to celebrate the Arctic's fluffiest apex predator. Zoos, schools, and conservation groups mark it with polar bear-themed events, and people are encouraged to cut their energy use to help protect the bears' icy home.
holidays.origin: Polar Bears International launched the observance to raise awareness of polar bears and the effects of a warming Arctic on their sea-ice habitat. It was chosen for late February, when mother bears and newborn cubs are emerging from their snow dens.
holidays.funFact: Polar bears look white, but their fur is actually transparent and hollow. Their skin underneath is black, which helps absorb warmth from the sun.

holidays.name: Pokémon Day
holidays.description: Trainers around the world celebrate Pikachu and the rest of the Pokémon universe. There are game updates, trading card releases, and a big announcement stream from the franchise.
holidays.origin: The day marks the anniversary of the release of the original Pokémon Red and Green games in Japan on February 27, 1996. The Pokémon Company now uses the date for yearly celebrations and announcements.
holidays.funFact: The first games shipped on Nintendo's Game Boy. The franchise has since grown into one of the best-selling media franchises of all time.

holidays.name: National Kahlúa Day
holidays.description: A toast to the sweet, rich Mexican coffee liqueur behind White Russians, Mudslides, and many a dessert. Fans mix cocktails, pour it over ice cream, or bake it into brownies.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial food and drink observance honoring Kahlúa, the coffee liqueur created in Veracruz, Mexico, in 1936.
holidays.funFact: Kahlúa is made with Mexican coffee beans, sugar, and rum. The brand's name is often said to come from a word meaning 'house of the Acolhua people.'
